Ritual Machines I and Ritual Machines II are phatic devices which aim to facilitate the accomplishment of family routines and activities at a distance. They are made from materials that can be found at home.
1. Mobile workers' practices of family life and work are shaped by a range of factors including the nature of work, family composition and the availability of technologies and services.

Ritual Machines I and Ritual Machines II are designed to support mobile workers and their families in the accomplishment of family life whilst travelling and to provide a platform for reflection on the values that families place in technology for supporting family life.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how mobile workers' lives are shaped by technology in the home, and the ways in which this is changing.
the design of technologies that are made to support the practices of families who live apart.
the role of digital technologies for supporting mobile workers and their families, with the design process for making a bespoke technology and with the values of making technology at home.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Ritual Machines project has provided us with a rich understanding of the challenges of supporting mobile workers in their domestic lives, and has enabled us to develop a design process which is responsive to the needs of this group and the values they place on technology for supporting family life.

this work has been a success in terms of providing a novel approach to the design and development of phatic devices and has been successful in terms of providing insight into the lives and practices of mobile workers.
the design of Ritual Machines I & II was an effective and useful method for understanding and exploring how families can use technology to support them in their everyday lives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of Ritual Machines I and Ritual Machines II was an attempt to understand how mobile workers' families accomplish mobile living.
we developed a bespoke design process for the design of a phatic device for mobile workers and their families.
Ritual Machines I & II are an exploration of how we might design for the domestic and mobile settings, through a process of making a technology with and for people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of technology to support families at a distance should be informed by the values of the families themselves.
we should consider how to support the family in their everyday life and not the individual.
we can design for mobile work by designing for the domestic, and vice versa.
